new_learnings.text: When 80%+ of strategy pool is in cold sectors (semiconductors -1.73%), the correct V2 response is to shrink to the minority of neutral-sector candidates rather than force entries into familiar tech names. Skip ~65 semiconductor-related candidates, focus on 药明康德/中国巨石/恒逸石化 in three different non-tech sectors.
new_learnings.mechanism: Sector gravity: institutional flows dominate individual stock momentum when a sector rotates into the bottom 30%. Global AI/semi sell-off (费城半导体 -4.49%) creates persistent headwinds.

new_learnings.text: VCP SETUP at MA confluence (药明康德: all three MA distances <2%) is an unusually strong setup. VCP timing edge + MA anti-chase rule converging at same zone = rare 'spring coil' entry that historically precedes institutional accumulation.
new_learnings.mechanism: Multi-timeframe MA agreement means participants across horizons concur on value. Combined with VCP contraction, this is a low-risk directional setup.

new_learnings.text: High IV (>75%) does not mean freeze — it means selective deployment. 86% avg IV Rank with 3.5:1 breadth is not a panic regime. Deploy 15% (not 0%, not 50%), keep 84% cash, widen stops for IV whipsaws.
new_learnings.mechanism: IV throttles sizing, not decision-making. Strong breadth + high IV = normal sizing with wider stops, not cash-hoarding.

new_learnings.text: The consumer-tech seesaw rotation is the dominant narrative. Food/beverage surging on policy, semiconductors collapsing on global cycle fears. Multi-day forces suggest this persists — avoid cold side entirely.
new_learnings.mechanism: Driven by US chip contagion + Morgan Stanley memory peak call + China stimulus + institutional rebalancing from over-owned tech to under-owned consumer.

market_summary: Breadth 3.5:1 bullish, 86涨停/12跌停, but deeply divergent: consumer/food surging (食品饮料+2% intraday) vs semiconductors collapsing (费城半导体 -4.49% overnight, 科创50 -0.87%). IV extreme fear (avg rank 86.4%). Global AI sell-off contagion meets China consumption stimulus — clear sector rotation underway. Deploying 15% into 3 non-tech names, holding 84% cash.
